topicName: Pod Security Standards and Pod Security Admission (PSA)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Pod Security Standards and Pod Security Admission (PSA) in Kubernetes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pod Security Standards define out-of-the-box security levels for Kubernetes pods. Combined with Pod Security Admission (PSA), a built-in admission controller introduced in Kubernetes 1.23, clusters can automatically enforce these security profiles at the namespace level without needing external third-party webhooks."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Three Pod Security Levels"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Privileged: Unrestricted policy, providing the widest possible level of permissions. It allows known privilege escalations and is designed for system workloads."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Baseline: Minimally restrictive policy aimed at preventing known privilege escalations. It restricts known dangerous configurations such as running privileged containers or accessing host namespaces."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Restricted: Heavily restricted policy following current Kubernetes hardening best practices. It enforces features like read-only root filesystems, dropping all capabilities, and preventing execution as root."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Modes of Pod Security Admission"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"When configuring PSA on a namespace, you can apply one or more of the following modes to dictate how violations are handled:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"enforce: Policy violations will reject the pod creation request outright."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"audit: Policy violations trigger an audit annotation added to the event recorded in the audit log, but the pod is allowed."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"warn: Policy violations trigger a user-facing warning in the CLI output, but the pod is allowed."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring PSA via Namespace Labels"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The primary way to configure Pod Security Admission is by applying specific labels to namespaces. Below is an example of a namespace configured to enforce the baseline standard while generating warnings and audit logs for the restricted standard."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: secure-workloads
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: latest
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn-version: latest
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit-version: latest"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Testing the Admission Controller"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To see PSA in action, try deploying a non-compliant pod into the secure-workloads namespace. The following pod specification attempts to run a container in privileged mode, which violates the baseline standard."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsafe-pod
  namespace: secure-workloads
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx
    securityContext:
      privileged: true"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you apply this configuration using 'kubectl apply -f pod.yaml', the API server will reject the request with a detailed validation error message explaining which security rule was breached."}]
